The paper uses eight class tokens and four for each other condition. With five scalar conditions (two times, guidance scale, lower interval bound, upper interval bound), that is 28 condition tokens. For a 32×32×4 latent and 2×2 patches, there are 256 image tokens, giving 284 tokens before transformer processing. This shape calculation is a reconstruction of those stated settings, not a universal iMF shape.

After attention and token MLP blocks, only image tokens are projected to the average-velocity latent grid. The practical auxiliary v-head is used during training and can be omitted for inference. The boundary-call alternative needs no extra head.

The auxiliary branch shares most of the network but has its own last eight layers in the paper’s implementation. It needs an explicit velocity loss: stopping the JVP also stops learning through that route. The added loss supervises the v-head; the branch is discarded when generating with u alone.

Removing modulation parameters can reduce parameter count while extra tokens increase attention work. Fewer parameters therefore does not mean proportionally faster inference. The paper also studies updated transformer blocks and longer training; account for those when attributing gains.

The upgraded transformer recipe includes RMSNorm (normalize using root-mean-square feature magnitude), SwiGLU (a learned gate controls an MLP’s feature channel), and RoPE (rotate query/key coordinates to encode position). These change block internals independently of adding context tokens. A residual block still adds its attention and MLP updates to the incoming features.

Condition scalars first pass through positional embeddings and a two-layer MLP; replicated tokens receive learned embeddings identifying their roles. Removing adaLN-zero does not remove careful initialization: the residual update has a learned per-channel scale initialized at zero, so each residual block initially acts like the identity. These details help make the architecture reconstructable beyond the top-level diagram.
sections.formula: [image tokens; class tokens; time tokens; guidance tokens] → transformer → image-token velocity projection

sections.title: 6. Read the evidence without turning it into a promise
body: The paper reports ImageNet 256×256, class-conditional generation with FID evaluated on 50,000 generated samples. Its system-level table lists original MF-XL/2 at 3.43 FID and iMF-XL/2 at 1.72 for one generator evaluation. These systems differ in architecture and compute; that comparison alone is not an isolated causal estimate of the new tangent rule.

Use the ablations for attribution: compare the objective change, guidance conditioning and in-context conditioning separately under the stated settings. Distinguish a reported benchmark from the analytic curves on this page. Our curves contain no reproduced image experiments.

One NFE counts one generator evaluation. It excludes the VAE decoder and says nothing by itself about training cost, memory or wall-clock latency. “Trained from scratch” concerns the flow generator; the image setup still uses a pretrained VAE representation.
sections.formula: Evidence: reported experiments ≠ mathematical guarantee ≠ this page’s toy output

architecture: x → encoder → noisy z → patch tokens
Illustrative /2 setup; token width stays D
Training v: boundary call or auxiliary head
JVP follows predicted v, not pair label
Decode latent; no JVP at inference
research: A useful ablation grid varies objective (MF/iMF), tangent source (boundary/auxiliary), and conditioning (modulation/context). Match budgets and evaluate more than one random seed. Do not change all three and attribute gains to one.

Possible thesis question, not a novelty claim: does tangent-estimation error interact with jump length or guidance strength? Measure boundary velocity error, JVP magnitude, interval-composition error, image quality, diversity and latency.

Before proposing a new method, read related work and search for prior art. State a falsifiable hypothesis, include matched baselines, and use held-out evaluation. The small scalar fit here can expose a sign or gradient mistake, but cannot validate a generative-model contribution.
